summary: Independent visual review of the 13 mask-audit overlays: is the no-envelope call right, and are there ring-bearing non-germline blocks?

reviews.magenta_description: There are 6 magenta objects, all inside the dense distal column (mitotic/transition zone) on the left side of the field: a touching pair at roughly (185,605)/(170,630), singles at (165,705), (215,720), (185,775), and one at the bend (245,840) (displayed-image coordinates). None is in a sperm/spermatheca location (the spermatheca is off-field beyond the oocytes at top right). In DAPI each magenta object is a nucleus-sized, textured chromatin blob identical in brightness and texture to its neighbours; none is a small condensed bright sperm/spermatid dot and there is no sperm mass anywhere in the field. I inverted the semi-transparent magenta blend to see the underlying LMN-1 pixels: each of the 6 sits on a round LMN-1 ring continuous with the surrounding field of rings (partial ring arcs are also visible at the margins of several fills without any processing). So the magenta fill is on real, ring-bearing germline nuclei, not on junk.
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: Almost all in the loop/bend region at lower-left where the distal column meets the horizontal pachytene arm (displayed x 180-450, y 850-1050): about 10-11 red and blue-outlined fragments drawn around black gaps BETWEEN nuclei (no DAPI, no lamin), including one large red-outlined black gap in the centre of the bend, several irregular red/blue slivers, and 4-5 tiny blue-only crescents/loops. Plus 1 tiny red-outlined dim speck above the distal tip (displayed ~(210,390), outside the gonad), and 1 small red-outlined dark crevice inside the top of the distal column (~(230,505)). None of these was filled magenta.
reviews.block_description: Not a second arm or another worm, but two large isolated somatic-looking nuclei outside the tube are outlined red and included: (1) top-left, a kidney-shaped nucleus at displayed ~(190-260, 280-350) with a faint LMN-1 rim and diffuse speckled DAPI; it belongs to a cluster of three similar large faint-lamin nuclei at top-left (the other two at ~(100-200, 200-300) are unlabelled) plus some bright lamin-positive specks; (2) a large oval nucleus at ~(40-110, 630-720), about twice the diameter of a germline nucleus, faint lamin rim, speckled DAPI, pressed against the outside of the distal column. Both look like intestinal/somatic nuclei, not germline. No sperm block, no second gonad arm.
reviews.notes: Split verdict on the arm. The spaced pachytene-to-diplotene arm along the bottom and up the right side IS clean: one red outline per ring, red edges present between touching nuclei, no magenta, no missed rings. But the dense distal column (mitotic/TZ, the most tightly packed tube of uniform round rings, displayed x 130-280, y 400-850) is NOT individually segmented: it carries a single red perimeter outline with essentially no interior red boundaries (I counted ~106 red pixels in a 90x160 interior patch vs ~689 in a same-sized pachytene patch), so the whole distal zone appears to be one or a few giant merged labels, and all 6 magenta fills sit inside it. If nucleus counts or per-nucleus metrics are taken from this mask, the distal zone would contribute ~1 object instead of ~60-80. Other issues: the three largest proximal oocyte nuclei at the top of the right arm (displayed ~(550-720, 110-200)) are over-split by internal red/blue boundaries into 2-4 labels each, and the first carries a yellow (unlabelled lamin) piece; the DAPI (blue) masks there are crescent-shaped diakinesis chromosomes. A second yellow outline sits in the distal column (~(225,515)), a small missed region between rings. The magenta test itself did the opposite of its purpose here: it flagged 6 real nuclei and missed ~12 gap/debris fragments in the bend. Two large somatic nuclei outside the tube are included in the mask (see block description).

reviews.magenta_description: Four magenta objects, all in the proximal (spermatocyte/sperm) region at the bottom-centre-right of the field, just below where the arm ends. (a) One large irregular magenta blob (approx. x 750-780, y 955-975 on the left panel) sitting between two ring-bearing spermatocytes; in DAPI it is a moderately bright, smeared, non-round mass (looks like a clump of spermatids or a squashed/apoptotic condensed body), and in LMN-1 there is no envelope at all on it. Its red watershed outline is larger than the magenta blue label and includes empty black space, so the whole label is junk. (b) A pair of small magenta dots (approx. x 700-715, y 940-950); in DAPI they are two tiny very bright condensed dots identical to the ~25-30 unlabelled sperm/spermatid dots scattered around them, no lamin signal. (c) One small magenta dot with a thin red halo (approx. x 685, y 960); same tiny bright condensed DAPI dot, no lamin ring. None of the four shows any LMN-1 ring.
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: Only candidate: at the bottom-centre block (approx. x 655-670, y 1120-1135 left panel) there is a small jagged, spiky red watershed fragment stuck to the top-left corner of a large blocky nucleus; it contains no lamin ring and only faint DAPI, so it is a watershed sliver rather than a nucleus. Everything else that has a red/blue outline and lacks a proper ring is lamin-FILLED rather than ring-less: about 6-8 small, saturated white LMN-1 blobs at the proximal end (approx. x 695-760, y 990-1050) that in DAPI are textured grey nuclei of spermatocyte size, i.e. probably dividing/diakinesis spermatocytes with intense lamin, not sperm, so I did not count them as junk. The dozens of tiny bright sperm dots around the magenta objects carry no outline at all, so they were never labelled and do not count. 4-5 very bright, saturated condensed DAPI bodies inside the distal mitotic tip (approx. x 1470-1500, y 120-200 on the DAPI panel) are absorbed into neighbouring red outlines rather than being separate labels; likely mitotic/apoptotic germ cells, not flagged, but not separate junk labels either.
reviews.block_description: Bottom-centre of the field, below and to the left of the proximal spermatocyte cluster (approx. x 600-780, y 1110-1210 on the left panel, running off the bottom edge), there is a cluster of about 10 red-outlined nuclei that are clearly not germline: one very large blocky/lumpy nucleus, one elongated spindle-shaped one, and several medium round/oval ones, all with dim but visible LMN-1 rings and diffuse, grainy DAPI rather than the compact pachytene or bright spermatocyte pattern. They are spatially separate from the tube and look like somatic tissue (male somatic gonad / seminal vesicle or body cells). Further to the bottom-left (x 340-560, y 930-1100) there are additional dim somatic-looking nuclei with NO outline at all, plus two bright elongated ring nuclei outlined in yellow (missed, unlabelled), so that far-left tissue is mostly excluded already; the red-outlined block at bottom-centre is the one that is currently inside the analysis.
reviews.notes: The main arm (distal tip top-centre, down the long descending stretch, round the bend at left-centre, and along the lower diagonal to the proximal end) is masked well: essentially one red outline per lamin ring, red hugging each ring, no fragmented rings, and no magenta anywhere inside the tube. Where nuclei touch, the watershed boundary is a thin blue/red seam and looks correct. The 11 yellow (missed) outlines are all in the dense distal/mitotic-transition zone near the tip and the upper descending stretch, where rings overlap in the projection; these are missed germline nuclei, not junk, and are the main loss in this image. Panels are the same field but the right (DAPI) panel is not pixel-aligned with the left in x at the top vs bottom (offset roughly 850-950 px), so coordinates above refer to the left LMN-1 panel unless stated. Overall: the no-ring test removed only true sperm/spermatid material here; the bigger issue for this image is the somatic block at the bottom-centre being retained.

reviews.magenta_description: Exactly two magenta-filled objects, side by side, just outside the left edge of the gonad tube at the proximal end / loop region (lower-left of the arm, roughly x 530-545, y 815 in the left panel). In DAPI they are two small, compact, very bright dots identical in size and brightness to the loose cloud of ~25 scattered sperm/spermatid dots that lies immediately around them (between the tube edge and the spermatheca). In LMN-1 the same positions are pure black background with only the red/blue outline drawn around them: no ring, no lamin signal at all. Both are clearly sperm/spermatid dots, correctly flagged. The second magenta blob has a small lobed red outline trailing off it to the right that contains one more bright DAPI dot that is NOT filled (see unflagged junk).
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: (a) 1-2 near the magenta pair: the tail of the red outline attached to the second magenta blob encloses a further bright DAPI sperm dot with no lamin, and there is a tiny red-circled bright dot at the tube edge just right of the magenta pair (right panel ~x 1520, y 875); neither is filled. (b) ~12-14 small red and blue outlined fragments in the interstitial gaps of the distal tip / mitotic zone (top of the tube, y ~ 90-300 in the full image): little triangles, slivers and blue squiggles between packed nuclei that have no ring of their own (they sit over neighbouring nuclei's lamin so the ring test presumably passed). These are over-segmentation fragments rather than sperm; they would inflate nucleus counts slightly but are small. No outlines at all were placed on the big spermatheca sperm mass (bottom right) or on the loose sperm cloud, so those are not a problem.
reviews.block_description: In the lower-left quadrant of both panels, below and left of the proximal end of the tube, there is a separate V/Y-shaped array of ~13 red-outlined nuclei spaced well apart along a faint grey haze of tissue (visible in LMN-1 as a dim V-shaped background), running from about (400,840) down to (470,1080) in the left panel. Every one has a clear bright LMN-1 ring (ovals and teardrops, several with very strong lamin, one small bright compact lamin object with almost no DAPI). In DAPI they are diffuse, moderately bright, granular nuclei with no condensed bivalents, so they are not diakinesis oocytes and not pachytene; given their position between the arm and the large sperm mass (spermatheca/uterus, bottom right in DAPI, no outlines) they look like somatic spermathecal / uterine / sheath nuclei. Two of them carry odd internal red outlines (a lobed inner contour and a hole-shaped contour). They are physically discontinuous with the pachytene tube and should be excluded from germline counts, but the audit treats them as valid nuclei.
reviews.notes: The crescent of pachytene nuclei (from the bend up to the transition zone, roughly y 450-850) is cleanly segmented: one red outline per lamin ring, no magenta inside, outlines follow the rings well. Minor issues inside the arm: three small yellow outlines (a web-like yellow contour around one nucleus near (615,790), a small yellow polygon in an interstitial gap near (660,640), and a yellow sliver beside a very bright elongated lamin object at the left edge of the arm near (615,700) that itself is only partially outlined; that bright object is probably a sheath-cell or folded-envelope structure). Near the loop, a few bright sperm dots overlap the edges of red-outlined pachytene nuclei and are absorbed into those masks rather than being separate labels. The distal tip is denser and less clean (fragments listed above) but no magenta appears there. Overall: the automatic no-lamin test behaved correctly (2 flagged, both true sperm dots, 0 real nuclei removed); the two things worth fixing are the somatic/proximal block of ~13 ring-bearing nuclei that is not part of the germline tube and the small interstitial fragments in the distal tip.

reviews.magenta_description: Two magenta groups. (1) Top-left corner: a contiguous mass of roughly 35-45 large filled blobs (each ~1.5-2x a pachytene nucleus diameter). In DAPI they are smooth, homogeneous, bright, rounded blobs, many fused into one lump; they do not look like sperm dots. In LMN-1 the region shows no ring structures at all, only faint diffuse haze; the red watershed outlines there form a chaotic web rather than ring-shaped contours, consistent with diffuse signal, not envelopes. The fill is opaque so rings under it cannot be checked directly, but no ring fragments are visible at the edges of any filled blob. Likely embryos/eggs or a degenerating clump; either way no ring. (2) Centre of the field (just right of where the loose proximal nuclei join the arm): ~40-45 small magenta dots. In DAPI these are small, very bright, condensed dots identical to the unlabelled sperm dots immediately to their right (spermatheca sperm mass). In LMN-1 there is no ring under any of them. A few dots sit on the rim of adjacent real ring-bearing nuclei, but the dots themselves are sperm, not the nuclei.
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: Immediately right/below the central magenta sperm cluster, in the gap between it and the loose column of bright condensed nuclei (display approx x 690-780, y 370-470): about 5-6 small red/blue outlined objects that are empty in LMN-1 (no ring) and are small bright dots in DAPI, i.e. sperm-like objects the test did not fill. One further object there (kidney-shaped bright DAPI) has only a faint partial ring and is ambiguous. Note also that the ~10 very bright condensed DAPI objects in that same column (running from the sperm cluster down-right) DO show small lamin rings, so they are correctly kept (likely apoptotic or condensed germ nuclei), not junk by the ring criterion.
reviews.block_description: Three things outside the main tube carry red outlines. (a) Left side of the panel: a vertical column of ~12 large round nuclei (large rings, speckled/spotty DAPI, intestine-like) sitting in a faint tissue band to the left of the gonad; about 5-6 are outlined red (e.g. the large oval with bright DAPI dots at mid-left, and several round ones above and below it), the rest only have small yellow outlines inside and no label. These are somatic and would be counted as nuclei. (b) Top / top-right: a loose arc of ~50 medium ring-bearing nuclei with textured DAPI, running from the top-left mass down toward the sperm cluster, plus a row of larger round rings further right (display x 700-830, y 270-300). All outlined red. They are not in the dense pachytene tube; they are most likely proximal somatic tissue (spermatheca/uterus wall) or the proximal part of the arm; unsure which. (c) One spindle-shaped flattened nucleus (sheath-like) at display ~ (790,505), outlined red.
reviews.notes: No magenta anywhere inside the pachytene arm, and the ring test did not remove any arm nuclei. Outlines in the arm are mostly one per ring, but several red outlines enclose 2-3 adjacent rings (separated only by internal blue Cellpose edges), and the lower third of the arm (display y ~950-1060) contains ~10 yellow shapes = lamin rings with no label (missed nuclei), so the arm is not strictly one-outline-per-ring. Magenta counts: legend says 89 flagged; I see them split roughly 40-45 in the top-left mass and 40-45 in the central sperm cluster. Real-nucleus-wrongly-magenta count of 1 reflects at most one or two small magenta dots overlapping the rim of ring-bearing nuclei at the sperm cluster edge; no whole ring-bearing nucleus is filled. The DAPI panel is drawn with a horizontal offset of about 957 px in the 2200 px original (not exactly half width), so overlays must be compared with that shift.

reviews.magenta_description: Three groups of magenta. (a) Top-left cluster, about 15-18 objects: in DAPI these are large, smooth, uniformly bright ovals and elongated rods (several larger than a pachytene nucleus, one very large round one ~2x pachytene size); in LMN-1 the same positions are completely black, no ring, no rim, nothing, and the red watershed outlines around them are loose jagged halos that clearly had no lamin edge to lock onto. They do not look like sperm (too big, smooth chromatin, not condensed dots), so they are probably nuclei of some other tissue or region where the lamin signal is absent; either way they have zero lamin envelope and removing them from a germline analysis is correct. (b) A small clump of 5-6 bright condensed round DAPI blobs at the upper-centre-left where the proximal cluster meets the transition zone (~x 430-490, y 230-270 in the left panel); no ring in LMN-1, just dark or faint diffuse grey. (c) About 6 small magenta bits scattered in the lower-left sperm field (~x 250-350, y 500-620): tiny bright DAPI dots, sperm/spermatid sized, no lamin at all. Nothing magenta shows a lamin ring.
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: (1) One tiny red-outlined object just outside the arm at the hairpin bend near the distal tip (left panel ~x 430, y 1020): a tiny bright DAPI speck with no ring. (2) Two or three red-outlined members of the condensed bright clump at the upper-centre-left next to the magenta group (b), ~x 450-500, y 250-290: bright condensed DAPI, only faint diffuse grey in LMN-1, no ring; the automatic test flagged the neighbouring blobs but not these. (3) Ambiguous: 2-3 small bright ovoid DAPI objects at the far left, ~x 210-250, y 380-440, outlined red/blue, that in LMN-1 show only a partial bright rim or crescent rather than a closed ring; could be spermatocytes with weak lamin. The many small bright condensed DAPI ovals in the lower-left field that carry outlines are NOT junk: at high zoom each has a thin closed lamin ring in the left panel (spermatocyte-like), so the test was right to keep them.
reviews.block_description: There is somatic tissue, but it is not red-outlined. Upper-right / right-centre (~x 690-900, y 230-480) a faint sheet of lamin-textured tissue outside the gonad carries 5 large nuclei with punctate lamin: 4 are yellow (lamin ring, no label, so excluded) and the fifth, the largest round one at ~x 870, y 370, has no outline at all. At the far left, ~x 170-300, y 120-250, there are 4-5 large irregular nuclei with granular lamin and dim DAPI that have no outline of any colour. Both groups are excluded from the analysis, which is the desired outcome. The only red-outlined large non-pachytene nuclei are 2-3 big diffuse-lamin, grey-textured nuclei at the upper-left edge of the proximal cluster (~x 290-340, y 280-300) which could be somatic gonad (seminal vesicle / vas deferens) but sit contiguous with the gonad, so I would not call them a separate block.
reviews.notes: The pachytene arm (right-side vertical tube, the lower horizontal segment and the distal tip at bottom-left) has no magenta at all, and essentially every ring has a single red outline that follows the ring; blue outlines are almost always hidden. Caveats: about 10-11 yellow outlines (lamin ring with no label) sit inside the arm, concentrated in the densest part of the lower horizontal segment (~x 650-730, y 850-890 and ~x 800, y 860) and in the distal tip column (~x 350-400, y 950-1050); these are missed nuclei, not wrong masks. A few blue edges are visible in the densest lower segment where DAPI labels and lamin watershed disagree slightly. Regarding question 2: two magenta bits overlap ring-bearing nuclei (one at ~x 290, y 490, one at ~x 275, y 375 in the left panel), but in DAPI each magenta piece is a small bright sperm dot lying on top of the nucleus in the projection, and the nucleus itself keeps its own intact red outline, so I do not count them as removed nuclei; worth a check that the ring nucleus retains a label. Note the two panels are offset by 1032 px, not half the image width; I aligned crops using the magenta masks. Overlay title reports 11 yellow and 40 magenta objects, consistent with what I see.

reviews.magenta_description: The bulk of the 215 magenta objects form a fan-shaped mass in the top-centre of the field (left panel x~250-620, y~70-400). In DAPI they are bright, condensed, elongated or teardrop/comma-shaped bodies, many clustered in rosette-like groups, i.e. spermatids and budding spermatocyte-to-spermatid figures. In LMN-1 the same positions are essentially dark or show only faint diffuse haze; the red lamin-watershed outlines around them are large irregular blobs much bigger than the blue DAPI label, with no bright rim anywhere, so there is no envelope. The remaining magenta objects are scattered small round dots (sperm-sized) lying over the gap and over the edges of the pachytene arm (e.g. x~287,y~565; x~497,y~710; x~612,y~770; x~635,y~797; x~615,y~847; x~637,y~875; x~490,y~480 an irregular bright DAPI smear hanging below the spermatocyte clump). All of these are bright compact DAPI dots with nothing in the LMN-1 panel. The unlabelled field of hundreds of small bright DAPI dots (seminal vesicle sperm, right panel x~1150-1600, y~300-720) carries no outlines at all, so it is already excluded.
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: (1) Bottom-left of the loop, under the condensed-nucleus cluster where the lamin is bright and crumpled (left panel x~480-560, y~1000-1060): one or two small red/blue outlines sit on faint, non-ring lamin wisps (e.g. x~500,y~1030). (2) Within the grey spermatocyte clump directly below the spermatid fan (x~400-600, y~330-480): a few red-outlined mottled objects show only diffuse filled lamin rather than a discrete ring; these are probably meiotic-division spermatocytes with partially disassembled envelope, not debris, so I count at most 1-2 of them as questionable rather than junk. No obvious sperm-sized bright DAPI dot was left unflagged.
reviews.block_description: Yes, there is a distinct red-outlined block that is not part of the pachytene tube: a clump of ~35-45 nuclei sitting directly under the magenta spermatid fan in the top-centre of the left panel (x~330-600, y~320-480), separated from the distal end of the arm by a dark gap of roughly 60-100 px. In LMN-1 most of these are grey, filled, mottled discs with a faint rim; the lower fringe (x~450-600, y~400-480) has clearly bright rings and some folded/crumpled bright lamin. In DAPI they are grey, textured, medium-sized blobs (larger and dimmer than the sperm dots, not the uniform pachytene texture). Given they are contiguous with the spermatid mass and have this morphology, they look like primary spermatocytes / the meiotic-division zone at the proximal end of the same male gonad rather than somatic tissue or a second worm, so 'non-germline' is unsure. Additional non-tube ring-bearing objects: several bright, crumpled, lamin-rich nuclei with NO outline at all (left of the fan at x~200-230, y~120-220; two bright blobs in the centre at x~660,y~350 and x~740,y~380; two yellow-outlined large rings at x~360,y~410 and x~505,y~795 below the arm) that look somatic (sheath/vas deferens) and are correctly not in the analysis.
reviews.notes: The one borderline magenta object with a lamin ring is at x~365,y~430 (left panel): a bright, elongated lamin-positive object carries a yellow outline (unlabelled ring) in its upper half and a small magenta-filled label at its base; in DAPI that base is a bright sperm-sized dot, so it is most likely a sperm lying against a somatic nucleus, but it touches bright lamin so I count it as 1 possible wrong removal. A couple of magenta fills at the fan/spermatocyte boundary (x~430-470, y~360-400) sit on faint diffuse lamin haze but show no ring. Pachytene arm: one red outline per ring along the whole descending limb, the hairpin and the returning lower limb; 2 yellow (missed) rings inside the arm (x~235,y~535 near the distal end; x~615,y~720 mid-arm) and ~6 tiny magenta sperm dots overlapping the arm edges in projection, each with its own label so the ring outlines are intact. Some blue outline segments appear in the denser mid-arm stretch (x~550-700, y~680-760) where Cellpose and watershed disagree on boundaries, but nuclei are not merged. The condensed, bright, oval nuclei at the bottom-left end of the loop (x~500-700, y~900-1050) have clear lamin rims and are outlined individually; they look like diplotene/condensing spermatocytes and are legitimately kept. Note the scratchpad is shared with other concurrent subagents (files with generic names were overwritten mid-task); I used m009-prefixed crop files.

reviews.magenta_description: Magenta falls in three places. (a) Top-right sperm mass (both panels, upper right corner, ~x 780-1100 of each panel): large irregular magenta blobs plus many small ovoid magenta objects; in DAPI these are bright, mottled, condensed chromatin packed together (sperm/spermatid mass), and in LMN-1 the same footprints are dark with no ring, only dim gray signal from neighbouring cells. (b) Centre of the field along the inner limb of the loop (~x 330-560, y 500-740 in the left panel): a chain of large elongated/ovoid magenta bodies plus small round magenta dots; in DAPI they are bright, mottled, cigar-shaped condensed nuclei (look like dividing spermatocytes / karyosome-stage cells and spermatid buds), and in LMN-1 they are completely dark inside the red outline with no envelope ring at all. (c) Scattered singles along the upper arc of the loop (e.g. the big ovoid at ~x 415 y 290, small ones at ~x 340-470 y 385-430 and ~x 360-400 y 480-540) and a handful at the junction/bottom (~x 570-700, y 630-720 and ~x 585-600 y 850-935): bright ovoid DAPI, no ring in LMN-1. Overall the fill lands on condensed, ring-less objects. Caveat: the centre cluster (b) is almost certainly germline (post-pachytene dividing spermatocytes/spermatids) rather than debris; they lack lamin because the envelope has broken down, so removing them is correct for a 'lamin-ring nucleus' analysis but they are not junk.
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: Mostly in the top-right sperm mass: several red/blue-outlined gray objects (e.g. the chain at ~x 800-1000, y 240-300 and the lumpy objects at ~x 780-820, y 150-200 in the left panel) show only diffuse dim gray in LMN-1 rather than a crisp ring, while DAPI shows mottled mid-intensity chromatin; they may be late spermatocytes with residual lamin rather than true junk, so this is uncertain. One or two dim outlined objects along the upper arc (~x 440-520, y 220-330) also lack a clear ring. I did not find outlined bright condensed sperm dots that escaped the flag: the loose sperm dots at bottom-right of the DAPI panel are unlabelled (no outline), and the small outlined objects there do have small bright rings in LMN-1.
reviews.block_description: Bottom-centre/bottom-right of the field, below and to the right of where the pachytene arm ends (~x 450-800, y 780-1000 in the left panel): roughly 20-25 small, well separated round nuclei with bright crisp LMN-1 rings, each outlined red, sitting in a sea of unlabelled bright DAPI sperm dots (very visible in the right panel). Immediately left of them, just past the tail of the pachytene arm (~x 470-580, y 820-900), is a group of irregular, lobulated, very lamin-bright nuclei. Both groups look like proximal somatic tissue (seminal vesicle / vas deferens / body cells) rather than germline pachytene rings, and they are included in the red mask. Two larger gray cells at far bottom-right (~x 690-710, y 890-950) carry yellow inner outlines (lamin ring with no label) and also look somatic. The two panels also show only one dense pachytene arm; the upper arc of the loop is a sparse mix of variable nuclei plus sperm, so I do not see a second worm or second arm.
reviews.notes: The pachytene arm (left side, from the tip at ~x 30 y 380 down and around to ~x 450 y 930) is essentially one red outline per ring with no magenta inside it; the only marks are two small yellow outlines near the tip (~x 60 y 425 and ~x 85 y 530, a bright condensed DAPI object in the second) which are missed/unlabelled lamin rings, not removals. The two candidate wrongly-magenta cases: (1) a ring-bearing nucleus at ~x 680 y 690 (left panel) whose small central DAPI label is filled magenta while the ring is outlined red (looks like a nucleus with a condensed chromatin centre; only the inner label is flagged, not the ring), and (2) two small magenta blobs at ~x 590-605 y 790-800 that sit inside a lamin-positive hand-shaped cell; they may be sperm nuclei overlapping a somatic cell, so both are borderline. Counts are approximate from the max projection. Note that removing the centre-field magenta cluster removes real germline cells (dividing spermatocytes/spermatids), which is appropriate if the analysis is restricted to lamin-enveloped nuclei but should be stated explicitly.

reviews.magenta_description: All 10 magenta objects sit at the proximal (top) end of the gonad, inside or at the edge of the sperm mass. In DAPI the sperm region is a field of dozens of tiny bright condensed dots; 8 of the magenta objects are single small condensed dots of exactly that kind (round, uniformly bright, much smaller than any germline nucleus), scattered on the right half of the sperm zone and one at the far top-right. The other 2 are slightly larger: one at the top-left is a pair of fused condensed dots (spermatid pair) and one in the centre of the sperm zone is a compact bright condensed body about half the diameter of a spermatocyte. Both of these carry an irregular red watershed outline that sprawls over the diffuse patchy lamin haze of the sperm region, but in LMN-1 none of the 10 has any envelope ring, only dark background or faint granular haze.
reviews.unflagged_junk_where: One clear miss: a tiny, very bright condensed DAPI spot on the left edge of the arm about 55 percent down the image (just below the bend, adjacent to a normal ring nucleus), outlined red/blue with no lamin ring in LMN-1 (dark inside the outline); likely a sperm-like condensed body or apoptotic fragment. Three borderline cases at the top, in the spermatocyte-to-spermatid transition just below the sperm mass: two blue Cellpose labels with large irregular red watershed outlines on the left, and one blue label attached to a bright ring nucleus on the right. All three are bright compact round bodies in DAPI and show only a faint, dim circular lamin trace in LMN-1 (lamin dispersing), so the test kept them; a stricter threshold would drop them. Not counted as junk: a wrinkled bright-lamin irregular nucleus at the left edge mid-arm (probably a sheath cell), a small lamin-positive fragment at the right edge just below it, and a flat bright-lamin body at the distal tip (DTC-like); these have lamin signal, just not germline-type rings.
reviews.block_description: There is no second arm, second worm, or intestinal block. The field is a single gonad arm from sperm mass (top) to distal tip (bottom). The only non-germline ring-bearing objects are isolated singles: one wrinkled bright-lamin nucleus at the left edge of the tube about 55 percent down (sheath-cell-like, red outlined, DAPI shows a loose cluster of dim dots), a small bright lamin fragment at the right edge slightly below it (red outlined), and a flattened bright-lamin nucleus capping the distal end (DTC-like, red outlined). These are 2 to 3 objects, not a block.
reviews.notes: The dense pachytene tube (from roughly 30 percent down to the distal tip) has one red outline per round lamin ring with no magenta anywhere inside it; outlines follow the rings closely on both panels. No image showed magenta inside a pachytene arm.

- Missed junk is small and mostly proximal: unflagged sperm-sized dots beside the sperm clouds (herm 011, male 003, male 006), diffuse-lamin dividing spermatocytes that pass because filled lamin haze reads as a ring (male 002, male 003, male 001 large mass), and interstitial watershed fragments in the dense distal tip (herm 03, herm 08). The dividing-spermatocyte cases need a stated policy (count or drop) rather than a threshold change.
- The bigger contamination problem is ring-bearing non-germline tissue that passes the test and is red-outlined: 9 of 13 gonads. Worst: noHS male 003 (~50-60 seminal vesicle/vas deferens/intestinal nuclei), noHS male 006 (large merged somatic block plus hypodermal/muscle nuclei), HS male 010 (~20-25 crisp-ring somatic nuclei plus lobulated group), noHS herm 03 (~13 spermathecal/uterine nuclei), noHS male 002 (~15 large dim ovals), HS herm 011 (~6 intestinal plus a ~50-nucleus arc of uncertain identity), 0622 HS male 10 (~10 somatic), 0622 HS herm 08 (2 large intestinal-like nuclei). HS male 009 has a large red-outlined clump that is probably primary spermatocytes of the same gonad (germline, unsure). Clean of blocks: HS male 008, HS male 013, noHS herm 004, noHS male 001 (somatic nuclei present but yellow/unlabelled in 008 and 001).
- A spatial or morphological germline-tube exclusion (distance from the arm axis, ring size/shape, DAPI texture) is needed independently of the lamin test; the lamin test cannot separate somatic rings from germline rings.
- Yellow (ring, no label) objects are mostly missed germline nuclei in dense distal zones (typically 2-11 per arm, up to ~25 in noHS male 001 and 26 in noHS male 002 where they are rachis gaps rather than nuclei); they are excluded rather than contaminating, but they would be junk if ever rescued in the male 001/002 cases.
